## Purpose

Add an opt-in level-1 sleep mode that destroys the model's FULL CUDA graphs,
serves eagerly after memory is fully restored, and recaptures one graph shape
at each idle boundary. The default sleep path is unchanged.

This provides an optional memory/latency trade-off for deployments that release
GPU capacity while an engine sleeps. In a matched Qwen3.8-27B BF16 TP2 test
(35 capture shapes, 8 GiB KV cache per GPU), enabling this option increased
memory that a separate process could allocate and write by **0.193359375 GiB
per GPU**, from 92.1953125 to 92.388671875 GiB. Both runs used the same candidate
source, with the option off/on; both cycles on both GPUs had the same result.

Memory snapshots account for the difference: 0.142578125 GiB in the graph
private pool, 0.03125 GiB in cuBLAS workspace allocations, 0.00244140625 GiB
in persistent graph outputs, and 0.01708984375 GiB in cached free blocks.
This is the combined effect of the option; it is not a measurement of CUDA
graph executable memory alone.
The driver can retain physical allocations after graph destruction. The
option does not promise to reclaim all graph-related device memory.

#59160 offloads the graph pool while retaining graphs; #59909 releases that
pool without backing it up and retains graphs. A separate matched comparison
against #59909 found an additional 0.05078125 GiB/GPU reduction with this
option. For four prompts generating 16 tokens each, median first-generation
time after wake was 1.111 s versus 0.416 s, followed by 4.345 s of
client-observed recapture wait. Medians use the final three of four rounds;
the wait includes polling/RPCs. Post-recapture residency was equal.
Steady-state median sleep was 0.627 s versus 0.557 s and wake was 0.630 s
versus 0.641 s. First sleep was 12.058 s versus 12.017 s and is excluded from
those medians. These measurements describe extra sleep-time capacity and
its recovery cost, not a general throughput improvement.

## Behavior

- Enable with `VLLM_SLEEP_DISCARD_GRAPHS=1` and the V2 runner. Only level 1 is
  supported; partial wake does not resume scheduling or recapture.
- A completed request after wake enables idle recapture. Each idle boundary
  captures at most one configured shape, largest first. Continuous traffic can
  postpone completion. A request arriving during capture waits for that shape.
- Recapture reuses its capture stream and preserves cached pinned host buffers
  used for weight backups. It does not replace PyTorch's global functions.
- Graph retirement resets custom-allreduce graph registrations while retaining
  static registrations. Participating workers close peer mappings before any
  worker frees the corresponding cached storage.
- A recoverable single-worker allocation failure leaves execution eager until
  another full wake. Multi-worker capture failures terminate the executor:
  a peer may already be blocked inside a collective. Multiprocess and Ray RPCs
  use the configured execution timeout for capture, sleep and wake. The `uni`
  executor cannot interrupt a blocked CUDA operation.
- If graph-pool offloading is also requested, discard takes precedence; no
  cuMem graph pool is retained for discarded graphs.
- An engine failure ends pending synchronous and asynchronous management
  calls instead of leaving their futures unresolved.
- Failed destructive transitions prevent resume. Worker termination is initiated
  before the fatal engine error is propagated to clients.

## Scope

Linux/CUDA, unquantized models, cuMem sleep, V2, FULL or FULL_DECODE_ONLY graphs,
without `torch.compile` or asynchronous scheduling. The default model list is
Qwen3 dense and MoE. Other architectures require
`VLLM_SLEEP_DISCARD_GRAPHS_EXTRA_MODELS`; testing a text path does not establish
multimodal correctness.

Tensor and pipeline parallelism were validated. Data parallelism is permitted
by configuration, but a multi-data-parallel-group lifecycle result is not
included in this evidence. Expert parallelism is restricted to a single
data-parallel engine group. Context parallelism, EPLB,
encoder CUDA graphs, speculative decoding, LoRA, transfers, extra weight
offloaders and communicator suspension are rejected.

## Related work and dependencies

This branch includes the prerequisite fix from #59228 at
`85eac2a2102b42520017dd0f1f06719e2916c826`, authored by aoshen02, to fix
freeing cuMem allocations while asleep. That fix and its tests are a
prerequisite, not a new contribution of this PR. The prerequisite is kept in a separate commit with its original author.

#59537 caches a capture stream globally per device. This candidate currently
reuses a stream only within the opt-in graph-discard manager. Once #59537 is
available as a dependency, the local stream parameter and cache should be
removed in favor of that shared implementation. The overlap is explicit;
this revision does not silently change the default capture stream.

## Validation

Local validation results: 61 graph-manager/worker unit tests, 7 client failure
regressions, and 18 allocator tests passed. With the final #59228 native extension, Qwen3.8-27B completed TP2 20-cycle
checks with the default communication path, forced custom allreduce, and the
Ray executor: all three tests passed (485.61 s). These lifecycle tests use
four capture shapes; the capacity comparison uses 35. The forced custom
allreduce test recorded 69,800 calls per GPU.
Four-GPU TP4 and TP2/PP2 tests passed. Batch sizes 1, 2, and 8 with mixed input
lengths generated exactly 96 tokens per request and matched their references
before sleep, after wake, and after recapture. A partial-capture allocation
failure recovered eagerly and recaptured after the next sleep/wake.

Qwen3-30B-A3B TP2 expert parallelism passed with TritonExperts and PYNCCL.
The final #59228 extension passed three Qwen3.8-27B shutdown cases: single
GPU asleep, TP2 asleep, and TP2 after waking only weights. The final Qwen3.8-27B TP2 fault run passed all five phases (preparation,
warmup, capture, sleep and wake), checking worker exit before explicit
client shutdown. The test RPC timeout was 30 s; production defaults are
unchanged. These results
span explicitly recorded candidate revisions; allocator-dependent claims
require the rebuilt #59228 extension. No results from the removed
driver-reclamation experiment apply.

The local target environment is PyTorch 2.14.0+CUDA 13.0, Ray 2.56.1, and four
H20 GPUs. The main requested model is the local Qwen3.8-27B checkpoint, whose
configuration declares `Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration`. Small-model fault
tests supplement the large-model lifecycle tests.

The proposed Buildkite job runs the repository's sleep lifecycle tests on two
GPUs. It has not been run by upstream CI. Model-specific tests and four-GPU
tests have explicit hardware/checkpoint requirements.

## Disclosure

AI assistance was used for implementation, review, and test development.
The GPU results above are local validation, not upstream CI results.

## Reproducing the lifecycle checks

Use a CUDA build with the prerequisite allocator fix and the matching native
extensions. On a two-GPU host, with the model checkpoint available locally:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 VLLM_PLUGINS= \
VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn \
VLLM_SLEEP_DISCARD_GRAPHS_EXTRA_MODELS=Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration \
SLEEP_GRAPH_TEST_MODEL=/path/to/Qwen3.8-27B \
SLEEP_GRAPH_TEST_DTYPE=bfloat16 SLEEP_GRAPH_TEST_ROUNDS=20 \
SLEEP_GRAPH_TEST_GPU_MEMORY_UTILIZATION=0.8 \
SLEEP_GRAPH_TEST_RPC_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=30 \
python -m pytest tests/v1/cudagraph/test_sleep_graphs.py \
  -k test_graph_discard_sleep_tensor_parallel -q -s
```

This selects the default/custom-allreduce multiprocessing cases and the Ray
case. For the five failure phases, use the same environment with
`-k failure_terminates`. These are lifecycle checks, not the 35-shape capacity
measurement. Multi-node placement and multi-data-parallel-group lifecycle
are not claimed as validated by this revision.

 ## Limitation
 
+### Experimental graph discard and lazy recapture
+
+`VLLM_SLEEP_DISCARD_GRAPHS=1` destroys the model's CUDA graph executables
+before level-1 memory suspension. A complete wake resumes inference eagerly;
+after the first request completes, the engine captures at most one pending
+graph per idle iteration. Captured shapes become usable immediately. Other
+shapes continue eagerly. Ordinary sleep behavior is unchanged by default.
+When combined with `sleep_mode_offload_cudagraph`, graph discard takes
+precedence: graphs use a fresh ordinary graph pool after wake, with no retained
+graph-pool storage to back up. Graph-pool offloading remains unchanged when
+graph discard is disabled.
+
+```bash
+VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 VLLM_SLEEP_DISCARD_GRAPHS=1 \
+VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B \
+  --enable-sleep-mode --dtype float16 --max-model-len 256 \
+  --max-num-seqs 8 --max-num-batched-tokens 256 --no-async-scheduling \
+  --compilation-config '{"mode":0,"cudagraph_mode":"FULL","cudagraph_capture_sizes":[1,2,4,8]}'
+```

+process and the `cumem` backend. Tensor, data and pipeline parallelism are
+supported through the `uni`, `mp` and `ray` executors, and expert parallelism
+is supported for MoE models (validated on single node with `mp`/`ray` TP2,
+`mp` DP2 and PP2, and MoE TP2 with and without expert parallelism; multi-node
+Ray placement shares the same executor path but is not yet exercised). Data
+parallelism requires sleeping through the async engine path, which fans sleep
+out to every engine core. Expert parallelism combined with data parallelism is
+rejected because the all2all groups then span engine cores with independent
+idle boundaries. Context parallelism (prefill and decode) and EPLB are
+rejected: decode context parallelism would need TP larger than the model's
+KV head count, and prefill context parallelism requires an MLA sparse backend.

+or FULL_DECODE_ONLY graphs and no `torch.compile` are covered by validation.

+`VLLM_SLEEP_DISCARD_GRAPHS_EXTRA_MODELS` environment variable at the user's
+own risk (validated once on H20 with the hybrid linear-attention
+`Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration`, whose GDN backend resolves to
+FULL_DECODE_ONLY). Additional weight offloaders, KV transfer, microbatching,

+Under tensor parallelism, every rank discards and recaptures graphs in
+lockstep through the executor's collective RPCs: the graphs embed cross-rank
+collectives, so ranks must never diverge on graph availability. A capture failure in a multi-rank executor terminates the engine: peers may
+already be waiting in a collective, so one rank cannot recover independently.
+The multiprocess and Ray executors use
+`VLLM_EXECUTE_MODEL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` for capture, sleep and wake RPCs.
+The in-process (`uni`) executor cannot interrupt a blocked device operation.

+def _graph_snapshot(worker):
+    import weakref
+
+    import torch
+
+    manager = worker.model_runner.cudagraph_manager
+    if not hasattr(worker, "_test_graph_replays"):
+        worker._test_graph_replays = 0
+        worker._test_graph_objects = weakref.WeakSet()
+        worker._test_recapture_streams = set()
+        capture_one = worker.model_runner.capture_one_sleep_graph
+        forward = worker.model_runner.model.forward
+        worker._test_recapturing = False
+        worker._test_host_cache_flushes = 0
+        empty_host_cache = torch._C._host_emptyCache
+
+        def observe_host_cache_flush():
+            if worker._test_recapturing:
+                worker._test_host_cache_flushes += 1
+            return empty_host_cache()
+
+        torch._C._host_emptyCache = observe_host_cache_flush
+
+        def observe_forward(*args, **kwargs):
+            if worker._test_recapturing:
+                worker._test_recapture_streams.add(
+                    torch.cuda.current_stream().cuda_stream
+                )
+            return forward(*args, **kwargs)
+
+        def observe_capture():
+            worker._test_recapturing = True
+            try:
+                return capture_one()
+            finally:
+                worker._test_recapturing = False
+
+        worker.model_runner.model.forward = observe_forward
+        worker.model_runner.capture_one_sleep_graph = observe_capture
+        original = manager.run_fullgraph
+
+        def replay(desc):
+            worker._test_graph_replays += 1
+            return original(desc)
+
+        manager.run_fullgraph = replay
+        from vllm.distributed.parallel_state import get_tp_group
+
+        communicator = get_tp_group().device_communicator
+        custom_ar = getattr(communicator, "ca_comm", None)
+        worker._test_custom_ar_calls = 0
+        if custom_ar is not None and not custom_ar.disabled:
+            original_ar = custom_ar.custom_all_reduce
+
+            def all_reduce(input_):
+                result = original_ar(input_)
+                if result is not None:
+                    worker._test_custom_ar_calls += 1
+                return result
+
+            custom_ar.custom_all_reduce = all_reduce
+        # Observe graph release before the backend changes weight/KV mappings
+        # or creates CPU backups. Those operations can change driver residency.
+        backend = worker.sleep_mode_backend
+        suspend = backend.suspend
+        worker._test_before_suspend_free = None
+
+        def observe_suspend(level=1):
+            worker._test_before_suspend_free = torch.accelerator.get_memory_info()[0]
+            return suspend(level)
+
+        backend.suspend = observe_suspend

+    # objects, including their generator registrations, have been destroyed.
+    worker._test_graph_objects.update(manager.graphs.values())
+    return {

+        "graphs": len(manager.graphs),
+        "graph_objects": len(worker._test_graph_objects),
+        "uses_cumem_graph_pool": worker.vllm_config.use_cumem_cudagraph_pool,
+        "replays": worker._test_graph_replays,
+        "custom_ar_calls": worker._test_custom_ar_calls,
+        "recapture_streams": sorted(worker._test_recapture_streams),
+        "host_cache_flushes": worker._test_host_cache_flushes,
+        "injected_oom": getattr(worker, "_test_injected_oom", False),
+        "free_bytes": torch.accelerator.get_memory_info()[0],

+def _run_discard_recapture_rounds(

+            assert all(

+                return [rank["pid"] for rank in asleep]
+            llm.sleep(level=1)
+            tags = ["weights", "kv_cache"]
+            if iteration % 2:
+                tags.reverse()
+            llm.wake_up(tags=tags[:1])
+            assert all(rank["graphs"] == 0 for rank in snapshot())
+            started = time.perf_counter()
+            llm.wake_up(tags=tags[1:])
+            final_tag_wake_s = time.perf_counter() - started

+            assert all(
+                rank["replays"] == prev["replays"]
+                for rank, prev in zip(first, awake, strict=True)

+def _arm_recapture_failure(worker, phase):
+    import torch

+    from vllm.distributed.parallel_state import get_tp_group
+
+    if get_tp_group().rank_in_group != 1:
+        return
+    if phase in ("sleep", "wake"):
+
+        def fail_transition(*args, **kwargs):
+            raise RuntimeError("injected sleep graph transition failure")
+
+        if phase == "sleep":
+            worker.model_runner.cudagraph_manager.discard_full_graphs = fail_transition
+        else:
+            worker.sleep_mode_backend.resume = fail_transition
+        return
+    runner = worker.model_runner
+    capture = runner.capture_one_sleep_graph
+
+    def recapture():
+        if phase == "prepare":
+            raise torch.OutOfMemoryError("injected recapture preparation failure")
+        forward = runner.model.forward
+
+        def fail_forward(*args, **kwargs):
+            capturing = torch.cuda.is_current_stream_capturing()
+            if capturing == (phase == "capture"):
+                raise torch.OutOfMemoryError("injected recapture forward failure")
+            return forward(*args, **kwargs)
+
+        runner.model.forward = fail_forward
+        return capture()
+
+    runner.capture_one_sleep_graph = recapture

+    supported_models = VALIDATED_MODELS | envs.VLLM_SLEEP_DISCARD_GRAPHS_EXTRA_MODELS
+    if (
+        sys.platform != "linux"
+        or not current_platform.is_cuda()
+        or not envs.VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING
+        or not config.use_v2_model_runner
+        or not mc.enable_sleep_mode
+        or mc.sleep_mode_backend != "cumem"
+        or mc.enforce_eager
+        or mc.quantization is not None
+        or mc.enable_nccl_comm_suspend
+        or set(mc.architectures) - supported_models
+        or not mc.architectures
+        or pc.prefill_context_parallel_size != 1
+        or pc.decode_context_parallel_size != 1
+        or pc.enable_eplb
+        # Expert-parallel all2all groups span every DPxTP rank, so each
+        # engine core capturing/discarding on its own idle boundary would
+        # desynchronize the cross-engine collectives embedded in the graphs.
+        or (pc.enable_expert_parallel and pc.data_parallel_size != 1)
+        or pc.distributed_executor_backend not in ("uni", "mp", "ray")
+        or pc.worker_cls != "vllm.v1.worker.gpu_worker.Worker"
+        or pc.use_ubatching
+        or config.scheduler_config.async_scheduling
+        or cc.cudagraph_mode not in (CUDAGraphMode.FULL, CUDAGraphMode.FULL_DECODE_ONLY)
+        or cc.mode != CompilationMode.NONE
+        or cc.compile_sizes
+        or cc.cudagraph_mm_encoder
+        or config.lora_config is not None
+        or config.speculative_config is not None
+        or config.kv_transfer_config is not None
+        or config.weight_transfer_config is not None
+        or config.offload_config.uva.cpu_offload_gb
+        or config.offload_config.prefetch.offload_group_size
+        or os.environ.get("VLLM_SLEEP_OFFLOAD_CUDA_CONTEXT", "0") == "1"
+    ):
+        raise ValueError(
+            "Graph-discard sleep requires an unquantized Qwen3 model, "
+            "the V2 CUDA runner, the uni/mp/ray executor, cuMem sleep, FULL "
+            "or FULL_DECODE_ONLY graphs without torch.compile, and "
+            "synchronous scheduling. "
+            "Context parallelism, EPLB and expert parallelism combined with "
+            "data parallelism are rejected; tensor, data and pipeline "
+            "parallelism and expert parallelism are otherwise supported. "
+            "Encoder graphs, additional offloaders, adapters, "
+            "transfers and checkpointing are not supported. Unlisted "
+            "architectures can be opted in through "
+            "VLLM_SLEEP_DISCARD_GRAPHS_EXTRA_MODELS at your own risk."
+        )
+    untested = set(mc.architectures) - VALIDATED_MODELS
+    if untested:
+        logger.warning_once(
+            "Graph-discard sleep allows %s via "
+            "VLLM_SLEEP_DISCARD_GRAPHS_EXTRA_MODELS. These architectures are "
+            "not covered by local validation; correctness and memory behavior "
+            "are not guaranteed.",
+            ", ".join(sorted(untested)),
+        )

+    get_dp_group,

     get_pp_group,

+    model_parallel_is_initialized,

 )
@@ -296,9 +298,20 @@ def _restore_sleep_parameters(self, model: nn.Module) -> None:
         self._sleep_saved_parameters.clear()
 
     def sleep(self, level: int = 1) -> None:
+        if envs.VLLM_SLEEP_DISCARD_GRAPHS and level != 1:
+            raise ValueError("Graph-discard sleep supports level 1 only")
         torch.accelerator.synchronize()
         free_bytes_before_sleep = torch.accelerator.get_memory_info()[0]
 
+        if envs.VLLM_SLEEP_DISCARD_GRAPHS:
+            self.discard_sleep_graphs()
+            after_graphs = torch.accelerator.get_memory_info()[0]
+            logger.info(
+                "Free-memory change after graph destruction and allocator "
+                "cache cleanup, before allocator sleep: %d bytes",
+                after_graphs - free_bytes_before_sleep,
+            )
+
         # Save the buffers before level 2 sleep
         if level == 2:
             model = self.model_runner.model
@@ -363,6 +376,61 @@ def wake_up(self, tags: list[str] | None = None) -> None:
 
         self.synchronize_device()
 
+    def recapture_sleep_graph(self) -> tuple[bool, int]:
+        """Run only at an idle EngineCore boundary with all allocations awake.
+
+        Returns (failed, remaining). A single-worker allocation failure can
+        discard graphs and return failed=True. Multi-worker failures raise:
+        peers may be blocked in collectives and require executor termination.
+        """
+        runner = cast("GPUModelRunnerV2", self.model_runner)
+        assert runner.cudagraph_manager is not None
+        try:
+            return (False, runner.capture_one_sleep_graph())
+        except torch.OutOfMemoryError:
+            if self.parallel_config.world_size > 1:
+                # Peers may already be waiting in the next collective. A local
+                # device sync cannot establish recovery of the entire group;
+                # let the executor's bounded RPC fail and terminate the engine.
+                raise
+            # A successful sync distinguishes a recoverable allocation failure
+            # from a poisoned CUDA context. Unknown CUDA failures propagate.
+            self.synchronize_device()
+            self.discard_sleep_graphs()
+            logger.warning("Sleep graph recapture ran out of memory; staying eager")
+            return (True, 0)
+
+    def discard_sleep_graphs(self) -> None:
+        """Discard any (possibly partially recaptured) sleep graphs.
+
+        Called by every worker during sleep, or after a recoverable
+        single-worker capture failure. All graph execution must be finished.
+        """
+        runner = cast("GPUModelRunnerV2", self.model_runner)
+        if runner.cudagraph_manager is None:
+            return
+        runner.cudagraph_manager.discard_full_graphs()
+        if model_parallel_is_initialized():
+            # The executor has synchronized all ranks before destructive sleep.
+            # FULL graphs are gone, so their custom-allreduce registrations can
+            # be retired before releasing the graph pool's storage.
+            seen = set()
+            for group in (get_tp_group(), get_pp_group(), get_dp_group()):
+                communicator = group.device_communicator
+                custom_ar = getattr(communicator, "ca_comm", None)
+                if (
+                    custom_ar is not None
+                    and not custom_ar.disabled
+                    and id(custom_ar) not in seen
+                ):
+                    custom_ar.reset_graph_buffers()
+                    # All importers must close their graph IPC mappings before
+                    # any exporter can free the graph pool's cached allocation.
+                    group.barrier()
+                    seen.add(id(custom_ar))
+        gc.collect()
+        torch.accelerator.empty_cache()
+
     def discard(self, tags: tuple[str, ...]) -> None:
         if has_kv_transfer_group() and "kv_cache" in tags:
             get_kv_transfer_group().unregister_kv_caches()

That revision removed `VLLM_SLEEP_RECLAIM_GRAPH_MEMORY`, the device-capacity allocation experiment, and explicit global cuBLAS workspace clearing. These remain absent. The feature stays disabled by default.

The single-GPU checks at that revision used H20, driver 580.126.09 and PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130: 38 focused tests passed, plus 20 cycles each for Qwen3-0.6B BF16, Qwen3-8B FP16 and Qwen3-30B-A3B FP16. Those historical results do not describe the current parallelism coverage.

Shutdown while asleep and after a partial wake were subsequently tested with the rebuilt extension.

Destroying graph objects still does not guarantee that the CUDA driver returns every associated physical allocation. Current measured release and recovery latency are in the PR description; the earlier driver-reclamation figures are not results for this implementation. All these GPU results are local validation, not upstream CI.

Historical tensor-parallel update; the failure-recovery contract described here has been corrected in the current revision.

A multi-worker capture failure now terminates the executor instead of trying to converge individual ranks back to eager: a peer may already be blocked in a collective. Capture, sleep and wake use bounded multiprocess/Ray calls, and fatal transitions initiate executor cleanup before errors are propagated. Recoverable single-worker allocation failures may remain eager until the next full wake.

The earlier dispatch gating and missing-import fixes remain. Current validation supersedes the earlier two-GPU smoke results: Qwen3.8-27B TP2 completed 20 cycles each with default communication, forced custom allreduce and Ray 2.56.1. The opt-in configuration allows TP, DP and PP, with expert parallelism limited to a single DP engine group. Prefill/decode context parallelism, EPLB, EP combined with DP, and encoder CUDA graphs are rejected. FULL and FULL_DECODE_ONLY are accepted.

The default model allowlist is locally validated, not upstream-CI-validated. Other architectures require `VLLM_SLEEP_DISCARD_GRAPHS_EXTRA_MODELS`. Current Qwen3.8-27B results cover its text path, not multimodal inputs.

The updated evidence includes TP2 with multiprocessing and Ray, four-GPU TP4 and TP2/PP2, and Qwen3-30B-A3B TP2 expert parallelism with TritonExperts/PYNCCL. Multi-DP-group lifecycle and multi-node placement are not included in the current reproducible evidence set; configuration support should not be read as completed validation.

Current changes also address custom-allreduce registration retirement, peer-mapping teardown order, capture-stream reuse, pinned host cache preservation, and pending management calls after an engine failure. Revision `83457b7297d93fa02fc64a05e0c142a52b83abb2`

Updated the implementation and description after adversarial review and GPU validation.

The candidate revision changes the earlier failure-handling contract. A
multi-worker capture allocation failure terminates the executor instead of
attempting to recover one rank locally while peers may be waiting in a
collective. The regression injects failures during preparation, warmup and
capture, and also during sleep and wake; it checks worker exit before explicit
client cleanup.

The candidate also retires custom-allreduce graph registrations, preserves all
static registrations, and waits for peer mappings to close before releasing
storage. A separate test forces custom allreduce and asserts that it actually
runs, rather than relying on a configuration flag.

Repeated recapture exposed two additional costs: distinct warmup streams kept
separate cuBLAS workspaces, and the high-level capture context flushed pinned
host caches used by the next sleep. The candidate reuses the stream and uses
the low-level capture API during idle recapture, retaining synchronization and
exception cleanup without flushing host memory.

The revised memory evidence now matches this implementation. With
Qwen3.8-27B BF16 TP2, a separate process could allocate and write an additional
0.193359375 GiB/GPU while the engine slept, compared with the same candidate
with the option disabled. Memory snapshots account for this as graph private
pool storage, graph outputs, cuBLAS workspace differences and cached free
blocks. Source graphs and graph executables were destroyed, but the driver
retained some physical allocations; complete graph-memory reclamation is
not claimed.

Against #59909, a separate matched comparison measured an additional
0.05078125 GiB/GPU release. Four short requests took a median 1.111 s after
wake versus 0.416 s, followed by 4.345 s of client-observed recapture wait.

large-allocation driver-reclamation measurements do not describe this
revision and have been removed from its claimed results.

Further validation found a separate client-side failure: a pending management
RPC could wait forever after the output receiver stopped. The revision ends
those pending calls, handles cancellation and late replies, and has a real
27B capture-failure regression in addition to the client tests.

The sleep-time free fix from aoshen02's #59228 is included as an explicit
prerequisite in the local candidate; it is not reintroduced as an independent
fix. Stream reuse also overlaps #59537, which should replace the candidate's
local stream cache when integrated.

each with default communication, forced custom allreduce, and Ray. All three
tests passed in 485.61 s; the forced path recorded 69,800 calls per GPU.
These lifecycle checks use four capture shapes; the physical-capacity
comparison uses 35 shapes.
